answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand visibly in front of them. Each receives the Voting card set with that color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play, but keep your own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “puts their Player ID card upright in its plastic stand”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing. Keep your own Ambush card”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player voting turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed”; “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is necessary. Red is the sole Target because Red received the most votes (three versus two each); the player or players receiving the most votes are Targets, including ties.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they tied for the most votes, and with neither playing Ambush both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive that requirement.
answers.evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep a player alive.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.”

answers.answer: Red's Ambush does not count as a vote. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count as one, so Red and Yellow tie at one vote and both are Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red's Ambush succeeds and Red may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink survive.
answers.evidence: Three-player example: “Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives ... Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.”

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush lets the Target choose one of the players who voted for them to eliminate. They cannot eliminate all four voters, and cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “chooses one of the players who voted for them to eliminate. They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The Ambush fails, and the player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among only the survivors.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure table: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.” Resolve Ambush effects before counting survivors.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Those are four cards, not four points: each card has a value of 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “Gold Bars are cards, not points”; each card's value is “3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go; they may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card face down. When both are ready, they reveal their choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go”; “each chooses one ... face down”; “reveal both choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome, including those eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave those four bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.” Edge case: “Those final voters receive no consolation bar for that outcome.”

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Steal player receives all four central Gold Bar cards; the Share player receives none.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: Share player gets 0; Steal opponent gets 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Steal player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: Grab One & Go against Steal gives its player 1 and the opponent 3; “Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Share player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: Grab One & Go against Share gives its player 1 and the opponent 3; “Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar; two remain in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each receives one and the other two bars remain central”; “add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of a round after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; thresholds are “at least 25 points” for 6–9 and “at least 24 points” for 10–12; “the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: The tied leaders conduct another Final Showdown, and repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player has the highest gold point total. The summary says the source does not provide an arrangement for three or more tied qualifying players, but for exactly two, it requires the Showdown. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in the round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “If the highest qualifying totals are tied, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown. Repeat these Showdowns as necessary until a single player ... has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.”
